<PAST H1 SPAN 1>NONDISCLOSURE AGREEMENT /</PAST H1 SPAN 1>
<PAST H1 SPAN 2>CONDUCT POLICY</PAST H1 SPAN 2>
<PAST H1 SPAN 3>Recipient agrees that all information disclosed by the Company to Recipient, including without limitation information acquired by Recipient from Company employees or inspection of the Company’s property, relating to (without limitation) the Company’s products, designs, business plans, business opportunities, finances, research, development, know-how or personnel, and confidential information disclosed to the Company by third parties, shall be considered Confidential Information. </PAST H1 SPAN 3><PAST H1 SPAN 4>Recipient agrees to maintain the confidence of the Confidential Information and to prevent its unauthorized dissemination; provided however, that Confidential Information shall not include information which </PAST H1 SPAN 4><PAST H1 SPAN 5>(i) is now or subsequently becomes generally known or available by publication, commercial use or otherwise, through no fault of Recipient, </PAST H1 SPAN 5><PAST H1 SPAN 6>(ii) is known by Recipient at the time of disclosure, </PAST H1 SPAN 6><PAST H1 SPAN 7>(iii) is independently developed by Recipient without the use of any Confidential Information, </PAST H1 SPAN 7><PAST H1 SPAN 8>(iv) is lawfully obtained by Recipient from a third party without violation of a confidentiality obligation, or </PAST H1 SPAN 8><PAST H1 SPAN 9>(v) the Company agrees in writing may be disclosed by Recipient.</PAST H1 SPAN 9>
<PAST H1 SPAN 10>Recipient expressly agrees not to use the Confidential Information for purposes other than those necessary to consider the possibility of entering into a business relationship with the Company.</PAST H1 SPAN 10>
<PAST H1 SPAN 11>All Confidential Information remains the property of the Company and no license or other rights in the Confidential Information is granted hereby. </PAST H1 SPAN 11><PAST H1 SPAN 12>All information is provided “as is” and without any warranty, express, implied, or otherwise, regarding its accuracy or performance. </PAST H1 SPAN 12><PAST H1 SPAN 13>Recipient agrees to return to the Company immediately upon the Company’s written request all Confidential Information, including but not limited to all computer programs, documentation, notes, plans, drawings, and copies thereof. </PAST H1 SPAN 13><PAST H1 SPAN 14>Recipient agrees to comply with all United States export controls with respect to the Confidential Information.</PAST H1 SPAN 14>
<PAST H1 SPAN 15>Recipient hereby acknowledges that unauthorized disclosure or use of Confidential Information could cause irreparable harm and significant injury which may be difficult to ascertain. </PAST H1 SPAN 15><PAST H1 SPAN 16>Accordingly, Recipient agrees that the Company shall have the right to seek and obtain immediate injunctive relief from breaches of this Agreement, in addition to any other rights and remedies it may have.</PAST H1 SPAN 16>
<PAST H1 SPAN 17>This Agreement shall be governed by and construed and enforced in accordance with the laws of the State of California as they apply to contracts entered into and wholly to be performed in the State of California. </PAST H1 SPAN 17><PAST H1 SPAN 18>The federal and state courts within the State of California shall have exclusive jurisdiction to adjudicate any dispute arising out of this Agreement.</PAST H1 SPAN 18>
<PAST H1 SPAN 19>Prior to taking YOUR exam, you will be required to accept the terms and conditions of the VMware NONDISCLOSURE AGREEMENT (NDA). </PAST H1 SPAN 19><PAST H1 SPAN 20>You will view the agreement on screen before the exam starts. </PAST H1 SPAN 20><PAST H1 SPAN 21>If you choose NOT to agree to the NONDISCLOSURE AGREEMENT (NDA) after you select Begin Exam, your exam will be immediately cancelled and you will forfeit your exam fee.</PAST H1 SPAN 21>
<PAST H1 SPAN 22>BY CLICKING THE “YES, I AGREE” BUTTON ON THE EXAM ENTRY SCREEN, YOU STATE THAT YOU HAVE READ AND UNDERSTAND THIS AGREEMENT AND THAT YOU AGREE TO BE BOUND BY ITS TERMS AND CONDITIONS. </PAST H1 SPAN 22><PAST H1 SPAN 23>IF YOU SELECT THE "NO, I DO NOT AGREE" BUTTON, YOU WILL BE EXITED FROM THE EXAM.</PAST H1 SPAN 23>

<SPAN 1>THIS AGREEMENT </SPAN 1><SPAN 2>is made the …… day of ………………….in the year of ……</SPAN 2>
<SPAN 3>BETWEEN:-</SPAN 3>
<SPAN 4>(1) ………………………… </SPAN 4><SPAN 5>(disclosing party) of……………………………………</SPAN 5>
<SPAN 6>ABN: ………………………………………………………...</SPAN 6>
<SPAN 7>(2) EFCA Pty Ltd (receiving party) of 28 Blanche St, St Kilda, Victoria 3182</SPAN 7>
<SPAN 8>ABN: 15 120 483 650</SPAN 8>
<SPAN 9>WHEREAS:-</SPAN 9>
<SPAN 10>(A) The parties for their mutual benefit may have exchanged and wish further to exchange certain confidential information (including but not limited to trade secrets and proprietary know-how).</SPAN 10>
<SPAN 11>(B) The parties wish to define their rights with respect to the said information and protect the confidentiality thereof and proprietary features contained therein.</SPAN 11>
<SPAN 12>(C) Subject or purpose of agreement………………………………………………</SPAN 12>
<SPAN 13>IN CONSIDERATION of the undertakings given by the parties hereto the parties HEREBY AGREE as follows:</SPAN 13>
<SPAN 14>1. Definitions</SPAN 14>
<SPAN 15>In this Agreement:-</SPAN 15>
<SPAN 16>Confidential Information means any and all information which is now or at any time disclosed to one party by the other party and shall include without limitation, data, know-how, formulae, recipes, processes, designs and design rights, photographs, drawings, plans, intentions, product information, trade secrets, market opportunities, specifications, manufacturing data, which is disclosed to EFCA before or after the date of this Agreement but shall exclude any part of such information which:-</SPAN 16>
<SPAN 17>1.1 is or becomes in the public domain without breach of this Agreement by EFCA; or</SPAN 17>
<SPAN 18>1.2 EFCA can show:-</SPAN 18>
<SPAN 19>1.2.1 was in its possession or known to it by being in its use or being recorded in its files or computers or other recording media prior to receipt from the disclosing party and which was not previously acquired by EFCA from the disclosing party under an obligation or confidence, or</SPAN 19>
<SPAN 20>1.2.2 to have been developed by EFCA, or EFCA’s principals, at any time independently of any information disclosed to it by the disclosing party.</SPAN 20>
<SPAN 21>2. Handling of Confidential Information</SPAN 21>
<SPAN 22>EFCA shall maintain the disclosing party’s Confidential Information in confidence and shall exercise in relation thereto no lesser security measures and degree of care than those which the receiving party applies to its own confidential information and which EFCA warrants as providing adequate protection against unauthorised disclosure, copying or use. </SPAN 22><SPAN 23>EFCA shall ensure that disclosure of such Confidential Information is restricted to those employees or directors of EFCA and EFCA’s principals having the need to know the same. </SPAN 23><SPAN 24>Copies or reproductions shall not be made except to the extent reasonably necessary and all copies made shall be the property of the disclosing party.</SPAN 24>
<SPAN 25>3. Return of Confidential Information</SPAN 25>
<SPAN 26>3.1 EFCA shall:</SPAN 26>
<SPAN 27>3.1.1 immediately upon receipt of a written request from the disclosing part, return to the disclosing party all documents and materials (and all copies thereof) containing the disclosing party’s Confidential Information and certify in writing to the disclosing party that it has complied with the requirements of this sub-clause; and</SPAN 27>
<SPAN 28>3.1.2 notwithstanding the completion of any purpose for which any Confidential Information has been disclosed or the return of documents and materials as aforesaid, continue to the bound by the undertakings set out in clauses 2, 4 and 5.</SPAN 28>
<SPAN 29>4. Limitations and Warranty</SPAN 29>
<SPAN 30>4.1 EFCA shall:</SPAN 30>
<SPAN 31>4.1.1 not divulge the disclosing party’s Confidential Information, in whole or in part, to any third party; and</SPAN 31>
<SPAN 32>4.1.2 make no commercial use of the same or any part thereof without the prior written consent of the disclosing party. </SPAN 32><SPAN 33>Notwithstanding the foregoing, EFCA shall be entitled to make any disclosure required by law of the disclosing party’s Confidential Information provided that it gives the disclosing party not less than two business days’ notice of such disclosure.</SPAN 33>
<SPAN 34>4.2 </SPAN 34><SPAN 35>The disclosing party reserves all rights in its Confidential Information and no rights or obligations other than those expressly recited herein are granted or to be implied from this Agreement. </SPAN 35><SPAN 36>In particular, no licence is hereby granted directly or indirectly under any patent, invention, discovery, copyright or other industrial property right now or in the future held, made, obtained or licensable by the other party. </SPAN 36><SPAN 37>Nothing herein contained shall be deemed to impose on either party any obligation to give the other party the opportunity of giving a quotation or making a tender to the other party or to enter into any contract for services or for supply of goods and/or materials with the other party.</SPAN 37>
<SPAN 38>5. Confidentiality</SPAN 38>
<SPAN 39>EFCA agrees to keep the existence and nature of this Agreement confidential and not to use the same or the name of the disclosing party (or of any company in the Group of Companies of which the disclosing party forms part) in any publicity, advertisement or other disclosure with regard to this Agreement without the prior written consent of the disclosing party.</SPAN 39>
<SPAN 40>6. Notices</SPAN 40>
<SPAN 41>Any notice to be given under this Agreement shall be in writing and sent by facsimile transmission or sent by recorded delivery post to the receiving party at its business address as last notified in writing to the other party and shall be deemed to have been given on the date of the facsimile transmission or two days following that on which the notice was posted.</SPAN 41>
<SPAN 42>7. Variations</SPAN 42>
<SPAN 43>No variation, alteration or modification of this Agreement will be valid unless in writing signed by a duly authorised representative of both parties.</SPAN 43>
<SPAN 44>8. Non-Assignment</SPAN 44>
<SPAN 45>This Agreement is personal to the parties and shall not be assigned or otherwise transferred in whole or in part by either party without the prior written consent of the other party.</SPAN 45>
<SPAN 46>9. Entire Agreement, Governing Law and Jurisdiction</SPAN 46>
<SPAN 47>This Agreement constitutes the entire Agreement and understanding between the parties in respect of Confidential Information and supersedes all previous agreements, understandings and undertakings in such respect. </SPAN 47><SPAN 48>This Agreement cannot be changed except by written agreement between the parties. </SPAN 48><SPAN 49>The interpretation, construction and effect of this Agreement shall be enforced in accordance with the laws of the State of Victoria.</SPAN 49>
<SPAN 50>This agreement will be effective as of the date below, and continue for five (5) years.</SPAN 50>
<SPAN 51>Signed on behalf of ……………………………………</SPAN 51>
<SPAN 52>……………………………………………</SPAN 52>
<SPAN 53>Date ……………………………………</SPAN 53>
<SPAN 54>Witnessed by: ………………………………………………..</SPAN 54>
<SPAN 55>Signed on behalf of EFCA Pty Ltd</SPAN 55>
<SPAN 56>……………………………………………</SPAN 56>
<SPAN 57>Date ……………………………………</SPAN 57>
<SPAN 58>Witnessed by:………………………………………………..</SPAN 58>

guidance.inspection: Reconstruct the operative protected-information definition from its preamble, incorporated definitions, alternatives, exclusions, form rules, and linked conditions. Test explicit identification as a universal proposition: marking or identification required for every protected item supports it; reasonable-understanding, circumstances, nature, or automatic-inclusion alternatives oppose it; mere absence of a marking rule is unresolved. For technical-only scope, use subjects within the controlling definition, not unrelated recitals or uses; protected business, financial, marketing, personnel, customer, or operational information opposes it. Express oral or verbal coverage supports oral inclusion even when later confirmation is required. Cite all independently responsive definition members and necessary governing language.

For each proposition locate an operative permission, exclusion, restriction, ownership rule, or reservation, then verify actor, object, recipient class, purpose, polarity, conditions, and necessary preamble. Independent development and lawful third-party receipt are distinct exceptions; neither substitutes for the other. Sharing requires an operative disclosure or access rule, with any incorporated recipient definition: employees support employee sharing, named nonemployee advisers, agents, consultants, contractors, counsel, or representatives support third-party sharing, and an exclusive employee-only rule opposes nonemployee sharing. Limited use requires a use restriction; copying, disclosure, access, or a limited license alone does not decide it. No-licensing may follow from express no-right, no-license, ownership, or reservation language; access or evaluation alone is unresolved. Preserve independently responsive clauses.

Decide return or destruction, copy creation, post-disposition retention, and survival separately while reading each clause with its lead-in, trigger, alternatives, exceptions, and cross-references. Return-or-destruction requires a mandatory disposition tied in the operative rule to termination, expiration, completion, conclusion, rejection, or another stated end of the relationship; do not transfer a separate termination event into a request-only duty. Copy permission must be affirmative, including a necessary-purpose exception; a prohibition conditioned on later consent opposes permission, and archival persistence is not copy creation. Post-disposition possession requires an express retention exception; an unqualified duty covering all material or copies opposes it even when request-triggered. Survival requires an identified obligation continuing beyond an end event. Preserve all governing and independently responsive evidence.

Inspect the complete document separately for agreement secrecy, compelled-disclosure notice, personnel non-solicitation, and reverse engineering. Agreement secrecy is supported by an operative prohibition covering the agreement, its existence or terms, or discussions or negotiations; definition-based coverage also requires the linked secrecy duty. Compelled-disclosure notice requires legal, regulatory, governmental, judicial, subpoena, or administrative compulsion linked to notice, information, or consultation for the disclosing party; a bare disclosure exception is unresolved. Non-solicitation requires an operative restriction concerning the disclosing party's employees, officers, consultants, agents, or comparable personnel, with its lead-in, duration, consent terms, and exceptions; securities proxy solicitation and unrelated customer restrictions do not qualify. Reverse engineering requires an operative reverse-engineering, decompilation, or disassembly prohibition concerning protected information or an embodying object. Absence remains NotMentioned; preserve all responsive evidence.
